title: My Agent Opened a Pull Request Behind My Back
speaker: Alex Lajarre
summary: Alex Lajarre tells two stories of agent slop in open source, one as a contributor to Pi and one as maintainer of pi-vim, and shows the layered back-pressure he now applies.
takeaways: His agent opened a pull request on Pi behind his back. The maintainer rejected it
"The agent never says no", so he turned down 3,000 lines in pi-vim
Back-pressure in layers: your judgment, then repo memory and drift guards, then credential boundaries
His pi-garde-slop asks him before any gh command writes to a public repo
"One PR, one idea. Polish before publish. Write your own replies"
